%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] An effect that creates distortions on the helmet glass. A textured helmet will work independently of this option.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Motion blur - blurring of the image when turning the camera, playing motion scenes, or with fast-moving objects.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the factor by which the maximum visibility distance set in the current weather profile is multiplied. The range of this value is from 0.4 (slider minimum) to 1.5 (slider maximum). For example, the weather has a view distance of 150 meters set. At the slider's minimum you will see 60 meters, at maximum 225. ATTENTION! High view distance can greatly reduce performance on older PCs.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the detail of rendering and lighting of human, monster, and weapon models in the game. The further the slider, the more detailed they will be.

%c[yellow]Default: 0.5.\n%c[default] This setting regulates how densely the tufts of grass are rendered in the game. The further the slider, the closer together the grass elements will be rendered and the thicker it will be. ATTENTION! Excessive grass density leads to severe slowdowns; if you want to adjust this parameter, do so little by little, checking the result each time.

%c[yellow]Default: 100 m.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the maximum distance at which grass is rendered. The further the slider, the further the edge of the grass will be. The slider allows adjusting the distance in the range from 48 (standard distance) to 240 meters. ATTENTION! The game's grass rendering algorithm is such that increasing the grass radius increases the load on the video card exponentially. More or less acceptable values lie within 150-200 meters (middle of the slider).

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] This setting enables grass casting shadows from sunlight and other dynamic light sources. This setting now works - we fixed it. ATTENTION! The setting absolutely WRECKS performance. Do not use it with a large grass draw radius or high grass density!

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] This setting allows you to enable vertical synchronization, i.e. synchronization of the frame rate with the monitor's refresh rate. When enabled, the effect of slight horizontal displacement of parts of the screen during sharp mouse movements will disappear, but performance may decrease slightly.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.
%c[default] This setting switches the anti-aliasing type. Available are NVIDIA DLSS (Deep learning super sampling), AMD FSR3 (FidelityFX Super Resolution 3), TAA (Temporal anti-aliasing), SMAA (Subpixel Morphological AntiAliasing). 
 
NVIDIA DLSS (anti-aliasing with deep learning algorithms) is a revolutionary AI-based rendering technology that improves graphics quality through the use of specialized tensor cores in GeForce RTX video cards. In desktop and mobile video cards, the technology became available with the arrival of the RTX20 series. Anti-aliasing using DLSS gives a result superior in quality to MSAA 8x, while not causing performance drops. 
 
FSR is a less demanding and lower-quality analog from AMD. FSR3 is supported by AMD video cards from the RX 590 and newer, as well as NVIDIA video cards from the GTX 10 series and newer. 
 
For DLSS and FSR3, a quality setting appears below: native resolution or upscaling for more FPS.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting switches the type of sun shafts. Choose the one you like more.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the AO quality in the game. This effect, when enabled, calculates areas additionally shaded by model geometry, making the lighting more similar to lighting in the real world; half-shadows and shading from equipment elements, clothing, vehicle details, grass, and other small parts of geometry appear on models.

%c[yellow]Default: SSFX (SSS 23).
%c[default] How ambient occlusion is calculated: the darkening in corners, under objects and where surfaces meet.
SSFX (SSS 23): its own pass at reduced resolution, smoothed over several frames. The softest and usually the cheapest, and the only type the AO settings below work with ( strength, radius, resolution, specular occlusion, AO on direct light ).
GTAO (Ground Truth-based Ambient Occlusion): horizon-based, physically closer but noisier, no smoothing over frames.
SSDO (ScreenSpace Directional Occlusion): the older method, kept for comparison.
Needs a game restart.

%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] This setting regulates the enhanced surface relief effect using the Steep parallax mapping algorithm. This algorithm uses ray tracing in heightmap space to calculate relief, which gives a more realistic and higher-quality effect.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] This setting enables a component of the depth of field effect - eye focus on the weapon during reload.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] This setting enables a component of the depth of field effect - blurring of the screen edges when aiming.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] This setting enables the appearance of drops on the glass of helmets and gas masks during rain.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] The setting enables wetting of surfaces during rain.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] The setting enables puddles and reflections in them during rain.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Tessellation increases the quality of low-poly models of NPCs, monsters, the actor's hands, animated items (bottles, etc.). Angular models become more smoothed. %c[red] \nATTENTION! With the current actor hand models, this setting affects FPS!
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] The setting enables volumetric fog technology. It is used to simulate murky water, haze in low-lying areas, and similar effects.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] The higher the shadow map resolution - the sharper the shadows will be in the distance (more than ~15-20 meters from the protagonist - beyond the boundary of the near shadow cascade). To avoid a noticeable degradation of shadow quality at this boundary, it is recommended to set the resolution no lower than 4096x4096. The setting very strongly affects performance.
%c[yellow]Default: 67.5.\n%c[default] It makes sense to increase the field of view for wide monitors and depending on individual preferences.

%c[yellow]Default: 0.70.\n%c[default] The player's field of view. If the value is, for example, 0.45 or less (less than the middle of the slider), then the weapon will be closer; if the value is 0.65 or more (more than the middle of the slider), then the weapon will appear further away during play. It makes sense to tune individually for wide monitors and depending on FOV.\n%c[red]For correct weapon display in this mod, a value of 0.70 is recommended.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.
%c[default] If DLSS or FSR is enabled, this setting regulates the scaling of the image in the 3D scope to improve its clarity. %c[yellow] 
At a value of 1 the image is not scaled. %c[green] 
Optimal value: 2. %c[red] 
At values greater than 2, FPS may drop noticeably.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Pauses after loading a save until a key is pressed.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Renders the PDA as a 3D object.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Shows the HUD crosshair. It remains hidden on Master difficulty.

A more forgiving journey through the Zone. You take less damage, find more useful loot, pay less for repairs, recover more effectively, and face reduced mutant ranges and special-ability pressure. Some equipment requirements are also easier to satisfy. %c[yellow]Recommended for first-time players.%c[default]

The intended uncompromising experience. Damage is harsher, useful loot is scarcer, repairs are more expensive, recovery is weaker, and mutants use their full attack ranges and special abilities. Equipment requirements are stricter, and the HUD crosshair is unavailable. %c[yellow]Recommended for NLC veterans.%c[default]

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Shows distance to the aimed target.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Uses the round crosshair from early builds.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Hip-fire follows the weapon barrel instead of screen centre.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Switches weapon slots with the mouse wheel.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Hides items an NPC will not buy in trade windows.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Shows health, bleeding, radiation, drowsiness, and other status icons.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Shows dialogue icons in DSH menus.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Allows artefacts to disappear after death and reload with a 77% chance. Binoculars reduce the chance.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Enables the alternative magic box interface.

%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Health by body parts, fractures, pain, fainting and slowdown from leg wounds. Medicine is applied to a chosen body part: drag it onto the skeleton in the inventory or use the item menu. Off: the old health system, no skeleton in the inventory.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] The hero portrait in the PDA and dialogs follows the worn outfit. Off: the standard actor icon.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] After the scripted sleep at the exit of lab X-6 you are moved to the Sarcophagus. The storyline between Radar and the NPP is skipped.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Widens the field of view based on sprint speed.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF (hold).\n%c[default] OFF requires holding the sprint key; ON toggles hold breath with each press while aiming.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF (hold).\n%c[default] OFF requires holding the watch key; ON raises the watch with one press and lowers it with the next. Weapon slot and fire keys always lower it faster.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] When enabled, firing guns drains stamina and unaimed gunfire receives a large randomized accuracy penalty. Knife stamina use is unaffected.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Enables camera shake near gravitational anomalies.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] Contrast Adaptive Sharpening (CAS) from AMD FidelityFX. Restores sharpness lost to anti-aliasing and upscaling (DLSS, FSR3, TAA). Higher values give a sharper image; at 0 CAS is not applied.

%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] Adjusts the amount of camera inertia.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Displays the character's lower body in first-person view, matching the equipped outfit.

%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Hits can injure your arms and legs, concuss you on a head hit, wear down your artifact belt, shake the camera and play pain sounds. Good armour absorbs weak blows. Injuries show on the watch and are kept in saves. The rules and treatment are explained in PDA articles, which unlock as you meet each effect.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] A light screen effect during an adrenaline rush after a heavy hit. Its strength is set in game.options (AdrenalineFxStrength, 0..1).
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Replaces plain distance fog with height-based fog, so haze gathers near the ground and in lowlands. Most noticeable in overcast and foggy weather.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Removes visible color bands from smooth sky gradients. Almost no performance cost.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Adds screen-space bounced light: lit surfaces slightly tint nearby surfaces with their color. Subtle, but noticeably heavier on the GPU.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Uses cinematic ACES tonemapping. Changes the overall color rendition and contrast of the image.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Offsets shadows from the sun and dynamic lights more precisely. Reduces self-shadowing artifacts such as stripes and ripples on surfaces.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Adds small screen-space contact shadows from the sun where the regular shadow map lacks detail. Heavier on the GPU.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] Water drops appear on the weapon, hands and held items during rain.
%c[yellow]Default: profile setting.\n%c[default] Grass and the branches of bushes and trees bend when the player or nearby creatures move through them.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] The game captures the mouse and keyboard exclusively. Turn it off if you have problems with Alt+Tab, overlays or other programs' hotkeys.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] You cannot sprint while reloading, and cannot start a reload or switch ammo type while sprinting.

%c[yellow]Default: DLAA.\n%c[default] NVIDIA DLSS internal resolution. DLAA renders at native resolution for maximum quality. Quality, Balanced, Performance and Ultra Performance render at progressively lower internal resolutions for more FPS.

%c[yellow]Default: Default.
%c[default] NVIDIA DLSS model. Models the loaded DLSS library does not support are greyed out.
F - legacy CNN model.
J - less ghosting, more flicker.
K - 1st-gen transformer, the standard for DLAA, Quality and Balanced.
L - 2nd-gen transformer, sharper and slower (RTX 40+).
M - 2nd-gen transformer, like L but faster (RTX 40+).
Default - chosen by NVIDIA and the driver.

%c[yellow]Default: Native AA.\n%c[default] AMD FSR3 internal resolution. Native AA renders at native resolution for maximum quality. Quality, Balanced, Performance and Ultra Performance render at progressively lower internal resolutions for more FPS.

%c[yellow]Default: Shader.\n%c[default] Shader - modern sun lens flare computed by a shader. Classic - the old sprite flares defined in the weather settings. Only works while sun lens flares are enabled.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Heavy weapons and scopes slow the mouse by their own factor. Off keeps one true mouse sensitivity for every weapon; weapon weight then shows through the weapon's own inertia.

%c[yellow]Default: While aiming.
%c[default] Procedural weapon bobbing while walking and running. While it is active, the regular weapon walk animations do not play.
Off - regular weapon walk and run animations only.
Always - bobbing replaces the walk animations.
While aiming - bobbing only in ADS; regular animations play when not aiming.

Ambient occlusion. Choose AO type SSFX (SSS 23) and an AO quality above off ( game restart ). SSS 23 AO has its own resolution and is accumulated over several frames, so it is smoother and usually cheaper than SSDO. Strength 0 hides it.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] 1 = full resolution, 2 = half, 3 = third, 4 = quarter. Higher values are faster and softer. Takes effect when the settings are applied.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] How dark the occlusion gets. 0 = hidden, but the pass still runs: to remove its cost, pick another AO type or set AO quality to off. Changes immediately.
%c[yellow]Default: 2.5.\n%c[default] How far around each point occlusion is searched. Larger values give broader, softer shading in corners and under objects. Changes immediately.
Light reflected from lit surfaces brightens and tints nearby surfaces. The switch needs a game restart. Rendered at a reduced resolution and accumulated over several frames. Strength 0 hides it.
%c[yellow]Default: 6.\n%c[default] Divider of the screen resolution: 2 = half ... 8 = one eighth. Higher values are faster. Takes effect when the settings are applied.
%c[yellow]Default: 3.\n%c[default] Samples per pixel: 1 = 16, 2 = 24, 3 = 32. Takes effect after a game restart.

%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] Bounced light of your flashlight only, separate from the sun and lamps: lit walls softly brighten their surroundings in the torch colour, also underground. 0 = no flashlight bounce. Needs Indirect light. Changes immediately.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] Strength of the bounced light. 0 = hidden, but the pass still runs: to remove its cost, turn indirect lighting off. Changes immediately.

Small sun shadows where the shadow map lacks detail, accumulated over several frames for a stable, soft result; distant terrain gets extra shadow detail. The switch needs a game restart. Length 0 hides them.
%c[yellow]Default: 2.\n%c[default] Ray steps for the sun: 1 = 8, 2 = 12, 3 = 20 ( 4 or 6 for lamps ). Takes effect after a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Contact shadows from up to 8 nearby shadow-casting lamps and flashlights on grass, ground and the weapon in hands. Takes effect after a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] Length of the shadow rays, 0 = off. Changes immediately.
Colour variation: natural patches of drier and lusher grass, trees and bushes.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] 0 = off, 2 = strong. Changes immediately; turning it on from 0 needs a game restart.

Reflections rendered in a separate pass at reduced resolution and kept stable over several frames, animated wave height with parallax, wind ripples. The switch, reflection quality and parallax need a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] OFF: the previous water. Needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 2.\n%c[default] Divider of the screen resolution for the water reflections: 1 = full ... 4 = one quarter. Higher values are faster. Takes effect when the settings are applied.
%c[yellow]Default: 2.\n%c[default] Ray steps of the reflections: 1 = fast, 3 = most accurate. Needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 2.\n%c[default] Depth of the close waves: 0 = off, 3 = best. Needs a game restart.
Reflections on wet surfaces ( Advanced settings > Puddles and reflections ): kept stable while the camera moves, blurrier on rough surfaces.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Works when Puddles and reflections is on in the advanced settings. OFF: the previous reflections. Needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 0.5.\n%c[default] How much reflections blur on rough surfaces. 0 = sharp everywhere. Changes immediately.
%c[yellow]Default: 0.\n%c[default] Reflections on dry glossy surfaces too, without rain. 0 = only when surfaces are wet. Costs performance in dry weather. Changes immediately.
Sun shafts and light beams from lamps and flashlights rendered at a reduced resolution, then smoothed along object edges. Much faster with almost the same look.
%c[yellow]Default: 2.\n%c[default] Divider of the screen resolution: 1 = full ( previous method ), 2 = half, 4 = one quarter. Takes effect when the settings are applied.
Light scattering in fog: bright light softly glows through dense fog.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] Trees and bushes get the same dry and lush patches as the grass. 0 = off, 2 = strong. Changes immediately; turning it on from 0 needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Only tree and bush leaves are lit as foliage. Fences, nets and grates keep their own material. Changes immediately.
Glass on vehicles and objects refracts what is behind it, with a slight colour fringe and reflections at grazing angles. Weapon and HUD glass is not affected.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] OFF: the previous glass. Needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] Crevices and corners stop reflecting the sky, so wet and glossy surfaces look less plastic. 0 = previous behaviour. Works with SSS 23 AO. Changes immediately.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] 1 = full, 2 = half ( faster, slightly softer ). Takes effect when the settings are applied.

%c[yellow]Default: 0.3.\n%c[default] Ambient occlusion also softly shades direct sun and lamp light, so debris, crevices and objects stop looking like they float in full sun. 0 = off. Needs SSS ambient occlusion. Changes immediately.

%c[yellow]Default: 0.5.\n%c[default] The low ground fog breaks into slowly drifting patches of mist in hollows, swamps and fields. Follows the weather fog. 0 = off. Changes immediately; turning it on from 0 needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 0.5.\n%c[default] Fog towards the sun takes its warm colour. 0 = off. Changes immediately; turning it on from 0 needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 0.5.\n%c[default] Gusts travel across grass and trees instead of everything swaying in sync. 0 = off. Changes immediately; turning it on from 0 needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] The clouds in the sky cast moving shadows on the ground. Overcast weather shades more. 0 = off. Changes immediately; turning it on from 0 needs a game restart.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] Ripples spread around your feet and around moving NPCs and mutants in water and puddles. 0 = off. Changes immediately; turning it on from 0 needs a game restart.
Colour look of the final picture. Changes only the image, not the light levels the stealth reads.

%c[yellow]Default: NLC.\n%c[default] Neutral: as the weather and the shaders render it. NLC: more contrast, deeper and slightly cooler shadows. Cold: a touch blue and softly hazy, less yellow. Classic: strong contrast, warm highlights and cool shadows. Changes immediately.
%c[yellow]Default: 1.\n%c[default] On top of the look preset. Changes immediately.

%c[yellow]Default: 0.5.\n%c[default] Lower values keep grass off steep slopes and embankments ( also less grass to draw ). 1 = grass everywhere. Applies to grass built after the change: load a save to see it everywhere.
%c[yellow]Default: ON.\n%c[default] Reduces flickering highlights on detailed glossy and wet surfaces, most visible with TAA and DLSS. Needs a game restart.

Glow of items in your hands: detector screens, lamps and indicators.

Shows the image without the new effects, to compare before and after. Not saved as a quality setting.

%c[yellow]Default: OFF.\n%c[default] Shows the image without the new effects ( AO, indirect lighting, contact shadows, water, reflections, glass, fog scattering, colour variation; volumetric light at full resolution ) and without their cost, no restart needed. Turn it on and off to compare screenshots and FPS. The effects must be enabled first ( game restart ).

Your settings in this menu are kept and come back when you turn this switch off again ( game restart ). Unlike Hide new effects, it is remembered between game starts.
